about: NIP-CK reader vectors. Every checklist reader (buzz-cli, stall-judge, buzz-vim core) loads this file and must produce `expect` for each case. Readers trust the relay for signatures; owner and watcher are given below. Regenerate with gen.js; never hand-edit an event. `defaults` are the production defaults (owner = lucian, watcher = the fleet watcher seat); every reader asserts its built-in defaults equal them. The cases use the test keys in `owner`/`watchers`. Content never decides which version is selected; the header_content_*, contested_odd_content_*, contested_nonstandard_* and content_* cases carry odd content (see Content reading in NIP-CK.md). Besides the selection, `expect` states what a reader reads out of it: `mode` (the selected header's mode, null with no header) and `item_status` (selected item event id -> open|done|parked).

cases.name: one_driver_all_versions
cases.why: creator keeps both versions; newest wins

cases.name: one_driver_pruned
cases.why: relay kept only the newest version; same answer

cases.name: squatter_signs_creators_address
cases.why: judgebot repro: X signs a version of A's header (d names A) between A's versions; X is ignored

cases.name: squatter_newer_on_creators_address
cases.why: a newer version of A's header by X changes nothing

cases.name: second_list_is_contested
cases.why: X starts its own header (backdated before A's): no first-come, the channel is contested until the owner picks

cases.name: owner_picks
cases.why: the owner signs a version of A's header: A drives, owner's version is the newest

cases.name: creator_edits_after_owner
cases.why: A edits after the owner: A's newer version shows

cases.name: owner_newest_pick_wins
cases.why: the owner's newest header version names the driver

cases.name: owner_drives
cases.why: the owner can be the driver

cases.name: items_only_driver_or_owner
cases.why: A's item stands against X's newer done-flip; X's and B's own items are not on A's list; the owner's item is

cases.name: owner_edits_item
cases.why: the owner's version of A's item is newer than A's

cases.name: creator_edits_item_after_owner
cases.why: A's later version beats the owner's

cases.name: no_header_no_list
cases.why: items without an accepted header show nothing

cases.name: contested_hides_items
cases.why: a contested channel shows no items until the owner picks

cases.name: malformed_ignored
cases.why: d channel != h, a creator segment that is not a key, a type that disagrees with the kind, a bad item id: all ignored (so they cannot contest)

cases.name: watch_only_from_watcher
cases.why: the watcher's record stands; X's newer one is ignored

cases.name: noncanonical_header_d_ignored
cases.why: uppercase creator hex, an npub creator, extra segments: ignored even from the key they name, so they cannot contest; an owner version at an uppercase address is ignored too

cases.name: h_d_mismatch_ignored
cases.why: X's header names this channel in d but was sent to another channel (h, channel tag); ignored here

cases.name: noncanonical_item_d_ignored
cases.why: items with an uppercase creator, extra segments or the old creator-less address are ignored

cases.name: contested_not_running
cases.why: two ideating headers: contested, but nothing runs, so no ping

cases.name: contested_one_running
cases.why: one of the two contesting headers runs: contested_running

cases.name: owner_switches_driver
cases.why: the owner picked X, then B: X's items disappear, B's appear

cases.name: owner_switch_before
cases.why: same channel before the switch: X drives with its items

cases.name: driver_edit_newer_than_owner_pick
cases.why: the owner picked A at 400; A edits at 500 and X edits its own header at 700: A's content shows and A still drives

cases.name: owner_item_at_non_driver_address_hidden
cases.why: the owner's item version at X's address while A drives stays hidden

cases.name: header_content_odd_mode
cases.why: a header whose mode is neither ideating nor running still drives (reads as ideating); items with a non-number order, no updated_by, or wrong-typed fields all show

cases.name: header_content_empty
cases.why: an empty header content still drives; an empty item and a non-JSON item still show

cases.name: header_content_missing_fields
cases.why: a header with no fields still drives; an item with no fields and one whose content is a JSON array still show

cases.name: header_content_not_json
cases.why: a non-JSON header content still drives

cases.name: contested_odd_content_not_running
cases.why: an empty header and one whose mode is RUNNING still contest; neither reads as running

cases.name: contested_odd_content_one_running
cases.why: a non-JSON header still contests a running one

cases.name: channel_tag_not_h_ignored
cases.why: a header, an item and a watch whose channel tag differs from h (d and h agree): all ignored, so X cannot contest, A's item stays open and the older watch stands

cases.name: item_d_h_mismatch_ignored
cases.why: newer done versions of A's item aaaa0001 whose d names another channel than h (either way round) are ignored: the open version stands

cases.name: watch_d_h_mismatch_ignored
cases.why: newer watcher records whose d names another channel than h (either way round) are ignored

cases.name: watch_extra_segment_ignored
cases.why: newer watcher records with an extra segment or a trailing slash in d are ignored

cases.name: missing_checklist_type_ignored
cases.why: a header, an item and a watch with no checklist-type tag are ignored

cases.name: tie_header_lower_id_wins
cases.why: two versions of A's header at the same created_at: the lower id shows (and its mode)

cases.name: tie_header_lower_id_wins_reversed
cases.why: two versions of A's header at the same created_at: the lower id shows (and its mode) (events in the other order)

cases.name: tie_owner_and_creator_lower_id_wins
cases.why: the owner's and A's versions of A's header at the same created_at: the lower id shows; A drives either way

cases.name: tie_owner_and_creator_lower_id_wins_reversed
cases.why: the owner's and A's versions of A's header at the same created_at: the lower id shows; A drives either way (events in the other order)

cases.name: tie_owner_picks_lower_id_wins
cases.why: the owner signs headers at A's and X's addresses at the same created_at: the lower id names the driver

cases.name: tie_owner_picks_lower_id_wins_reversed
cases.why: the owner signs headers at A's and X's addresses at the same created_at: the lower id names the driver (events in the other order)

cases.name: tie_item_lower_id_wins
cases.why: two versions of an item by A, and the owner's and A's versions of another, each pair at the same created_at: the lower id shows (and its status)

cases.name: tie_item_lower_id_wins_reversed
cases.why: two versions of an item by A, and the owner's and A's versions of another, each pair at the same created_at: the lower id shows (and its status) (events in the other order)

cases.name: tie_watch_lower_id_wins
cases.why: two watcher records at the same created_at: the lower id stands

cases.name: tie_watch_lower_id_wins_reversed
cases.why: two watcher records at the same created_at: the lower id stands (events in the other order)

cases.name: content_nonstandard_numbers_unreadable
cases.why: Infinity, NaN, -Infinity and numbers past f64 (1e400, a 401-digit integer) make the content unreadable: the header reads as ideating and those items as open, but all still show; a large finite number reads normally

cases.name: contested_nonstandard_not_running
cases.why: a header with mode running and an Infinity elsewhere does not read as running, so this contest does not run

cases.name: content_lone_surrogate_unreadable
cases.why: a lone surrogate escape (in a value or a key) makes the content unreadable; a valid surrogate pair reads normally

cases.name: content_nesting_limit
cases.why: content nested 127 deep reads normally; 128 deep (serde_json's limit) or 5000 deep is unreadable and reads as {}

cases.name: content_duplicate_keys_last_wins
cases.why: a key given twice reads as its last value

cases.name: content_one_bad_field_keeps_the_rest
cases.why: wrong-typed fields beside a good mode or status: the mode and status still read
